new_full_body_scene.note: M2 is a proportion overview; its small face is not the face authority.

lower_body_detail.note: G2/P6 support construction only; keep the current grey socks from L1/G2.

existing_image_edit.support: Choose relevant IDs from the profiles above; preserve the target scene, pose and camera.
existing_image_edit.sock_material_note: If the target already carries the selected soft sock material, it can supply that material reference. For a socks-only correction use the target, native L1 and a selected material example with other relevant details as needed; preserve the target scene and camera.

usage_rules: Before generation, read README.md and reference-set.json, open the edit target and relevant native reference images with view_image, and assign each input an explicit role.

For a new full-body scene, use P1 for original face, eye design, black bob and drawing; P2 for the ordinary closed-mouth smile; native U1 for upper-body detail; and native L1 for lower-body detail. Add S1 for exact pin design and M2 for whole-body balance when needed.

P1 and P2 remain the original face/eye and expression authorities. Derived U1, G2 and M2 images do not replace them. Preserve the small distinct dark oval pupil, neutral grey iris zones and rounded pale lower-iris reflections from P1; do not enlarge the eyes to substitute for detail.
Use U1 and L1 as separate full-resolution inputs, not only a thumbnail, contact sheet or M2 montage. Small full-body display size still reduces visible eye pixels.
For an existing-image correction, the edit target remains the sole scene, camera and pose source; supporting references supply only their assigned character details.

For new split renders, establish one shared camera, pose, proportions and lighting first. Keep a generous overlapping waist/skirt region in both crops. The saved layout and masks reproduce this selected standing pose only.

When assembling parts, keep complete arms and hands from one input and put transitions within clothing/background. Prefer anatomical and object continuity; do not force geometric warps or cut across limbs to minimize pixel changes.
Use S1 for one bright silver slim straight pin with rounded tips, at the character-left temple just above the ear; viewer-right in these approved references.

L1 carries the G2 medium-neutral-grey opaque ribbed below-knee socks, healthy leg contours, blue-grey pleated skirt and white sneakers. G2 remains the approved source layout and sock-color origin; P6 is inherited construction support whose navy socks and absent pin are superseded.
Later situation or expression selections do not automatically change these roles. Use the current black-bob v3.0 lineage; do not mix v1/v2 or the August v3.0 research design into this version.

Use selected A16-E1-1 as the clothing-finish guide: group small internal shadows subtly while retaining major folds, dimensionality, seams and plaid. Treat it as clothing-finish support only; keep P1/P2 original face and expression authority, native U1/L1 detail roles and the current target scene, pose, camera and outfit. E2/E3 are not selected; transfer beyond A16 still needs visual review.

MUST preserve the selected soft opaque rib-knit sock material from F01/F02/F04/F05/F06 wherever sock fabric is visible: rounded fabric-covered toes when visible, soft connected shading, and natural posture-dependent ankle/contact folds. Use sock-material-requirement.json and prompts/sock-material-must.txt. Footwear may hide toes; do not force hidden details into view. New poses, actions and cameras are free to vary; these material examples do not replace P1/P2 or native U1/L1.
